points.description: Correct Tustin-discretised difference equation with numerical coefficients to 3 s.f.: y_k = 0.0591(u_k + u_{k-1}) + 0.882 y_{k-1} (b0 = b1 = κ/(1+κ) ≈ 0.0591, with κ = ωcT/2 = 0.0628, and a1 = (κ−1)/(1+κ) ≈ −0.882, i.e. +0.882 y_{k-1} on the right-hand side). Equivalent forms accepted (e.g. y_k − 0.882 y_{k-1} = 0.0591 u_k + 0.0591 u_{k-1}). Sign error on the y_{k-1} term or wrong coefficients earns no credit.

levels.says: Correct method (Tustin substitution with ωc = 125.66 rad/s, T = 1 ms) and correct general form of H(z), but numerical coefficients wrong or not given to 3 s.f.

points.description: DC gain verified by evaluating H(z) at z = 1 (or by setting y_k = y_{k-1}, u_k = u_{k-1} in the difference equation): (b0+b1)/(1+a1) = 0.1182/0.1182 = 1, so the gain is unity. Must show the evaluation, not just assert it. Follow-through is allowed using the student's own coefficients if they are consistent.

rubric.notes: Full marks for the correct difference equation with coefficients 0.0591 (both input terms) and 0.882 (feedback term), and for showing the z=1 evaluation giving a gain of exactly 1. Give half of P1 for a correct method with a numerical slip. A bare statement that the DC gain is 1 without evaluation earns nothing for P2.
